visual.general_description: Grayscale axial head CT slice with orientation letters and a 1 cm scale bar.
visual.detailed_description: Grayscale axial CT slice of the head at the level of the posterior fossa and temporal lobes. The skull is a bright rim around the brain; the cerebellum lies posteriorly, the temporal lobes laterally and the frontal lobes anteriorly with the midline falx visible. A few small bright foci lie near the midline in the central skull-base region, and black air-filled spaces with irregular bony margins lie behind the ears on both sides. The ears and scalp soft tissue are visible. Orientation letters "R" at the left of the image, "L" at the right and "P" at the bottom are printed, together with a vertical ruler scale labelled "1cm" at the right edge. No arrows, panel letters, patient text, dates or scanner text are visible.

visual.general_description: Grayscale sagittal brain MRI with a green arrow pointing to a rounded sellar lesion with a bright rim.
visual.detailed_description: Grayscale midsagittal MRI of the head showing the brain, corpus callosum, brainstem, cerebellum, and the facial and neck soft tissues. A green arrow in the lower-central region points to a rounded structure in the sellar region anterior to the brainstem, which has a bright peripheral rim and an intermediate-signal center. Printed letters "A" and "L" on the left, "P" and "R" on the right, "FL" at the bottom, and a vertical ruler labelled "1 cm" at the right edge. The profile of the nose, lips and chin is visible as soft-tissue outline. No panel letters, patient text, dates or scanner text are visible.
